entries.title: Numbers 6:2
segments: A Nazarite; the Nazarite was one specially consecrated to God by his parents or himself, and that either for life or for a limited term. See note to
.  In this chapter the case of those only whose Nazariteship continued for a limited time is considered.

entries.title: Numbers 6:4
segments: Eat nothing that is made of the vine-tree; this was a symbol of sobriety, and of abstinence from all the intoxicating pleasures of sin.

entries.title: Numbers 6:7
segments: He shall not make himself unclean; by approaching the dead body. The Jews add that he was required to abstain from the customary signs of mourning, as in the case of the high-priest.  This and all the other regulations were designed to impress upon his mind the sacredness of his peculiar relation to God, and the deadness to worldly joys and sorrows demanded by it.

entries.title: Numbers 6:8
segments: Holiness to the Lord is the badge of his people, and should ever be their peculiar characteristic.  They should abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul, moderate their desires for earthly things, place their affections on things above, and regulate all their acts by the will of God.

entries.title: Numbers 6:12
segments: Days--shall be lost; they would not be counted as a part of the time of his Nazariteship, but he must begin again.

entries.title: Numbers 6:14
segments: His offering; these offerings were an acknowledgment that in his best services he needed the efficacy of atoning blood and of the purifying Spirit, and also tokens of gratitude for the goodness of God.

entries.title: Numbers 6:15
segments: Meat-offering--drink-offerings; those accompanying the sacrifices mentioned in the preceding verse.  See

entries.title: Numbers 6:19
segments: Sodden shoulder; the boiled shoulder, which was the left shoulder, the right with the wave-breast having been given to the priest by a general law.

entries.title: Numbers 6:20
segments: We are always exposed in this world to moral defilement, and in our best services need the application of the blood of Christ and the purifying influences of his Spirit, in order that our offerings may be acceptable in his sight.

entries.title: Numbers 6:21
segments: That his hand shall get; such freewill-offerings as he shall be able to make.

entries.title: Numbers 6:24
segments:
vv 24-26. 
 
This three fold divine benediction is supposed by many interpreters to contain an intimation of the Trinity in the godhead.

entries.title: Numbers 6:27
segments:
Put my name; call Israel by my name, and teach them to obey me as my peculiar people. 
 
The blessing of Jehovah, in the love of the Father, the grace of the Son, and the communion of the Holy Ghost, bestowed upon his believing, obedient people, will make them all for ever truly and perfectly blessed.
